title: Schedule captures a halted clock configuration
statement: Let $W$ be a finite-state binary machine, let $a,b$ be natural numbers, and let $T:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. Suppose that on every Boolean input word $x$, $W$ halts within $b(T(|x|)+1)$ steps and outputs the binary representation of $T(|x|)$. For every such $x$, there are a time $\tau\le b(T(|x|)+1)$ and a halted configuration $c$ of $W$ on $x$ whose output is that binary representation, such that the length-only schedule machine, started on the bit-encoded input, reaches the clock-stage configuration associated with $c$ after $\tau+1$ steps.
hypotheses_covered: for every input x, W computes the binary representation of T(|x|) within b(T(|x|)+1) steps
configuration c is halted and has the specified output
